articles.title: BCCI Struggles To Find New Title Sponsor; Reason Will Surprise You
articles.description:
It may sound surprising that the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is struggling to find a title sponsor for the Indian cricket team’s home matches, but that is currently the case. The issue, however, is not a lack of interest in Indian cricket. Instead, the steep asking price for the sponsorship rights appears to be discouraging potential buyers.

BCCI invited bids for the title sponsorship rights, with August 13 set as the deadline for submissions. However, the board either received no bids or did not get offers that matched its expectations.

The tender process began on July 20, when BCCI issued its Invitation to Tender (ITT). Interested parties had until August 4 to purchase the tender documents, while August 5 was the deadline for submitting requests for clarification.

The board is reportedly still in discussions with several potential sponsors. Google Gemini is among the brands said to be involved in talks, while Spinny and SBI Life are also reportedly exploring the opportunity.

High Base Price Becomes Major Hurdle

The sponsorship rights were previously held by IDFC First Bank, which paid ₹4.2 crore per match. For the new cycle, however, the BCCI has increased the base price to ₹4.75 crore per match. This higher valuation is believed to be one of the key reasons potential sponsors have been reluctant to commit.

The new agreement is expected to run for two years, compared with the three-year deal secured by IDFC First Bank in 2023. The BCCI has estimated that around 35 matches could fall under the sponsorship period.

According to a report by Cricbuzz, BCCI has projected approximately 35 chargeable matches during the rights period, although the final number will depend on the schedule eventually approved by the board.

Several companies have nevertheless shown interest in exploring the property. The ITT documents reportedly carried a non-refundable fee of ₹1 lakh, with GroupM, ITW and Sporty Solutions among those said to have purchased the tender documents.

For now, BCCI continues to negotiate with prospective sponsors as it looks to finalise a title sponsor for India’s home international matches.

articles.title: IND vs SL 2nd Test Live: Toss Result And Confirmed Playing 11
articles.description:
IND vs SL 2nd Test Live: India won the toss and elected to bat first against Sri Lanka in the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo. Shubman Gill's side lead the two-match series 1-0 after a convincing 165-run victory in Galle.

India have made one change to their playing XI, with Saransh Jain handed his Test debut in place of Kuldeep Yadav, who misses the match due to an infection.

Sri Lanka have also named their confirmed XI as they look to level the series on home soil.

IND vs SL 2nd Test Toss Result

Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bat first in Colombo. The India captain said the surface looked harder and better for batting than the Galle pitch, particularly during the opening days.

India will hope to make the most of the conditions before the surface begins to slow down and offer more assistance to the spinners.

Gill also reflected positively on India's performance in the first Test, while acknowledging that his side still had areas to improve despite their dominant victory.

IND vs SL 2nd Test: Playing XI

India have retained most of their winning combination from the first Test, with Saransh Jain coming into the side for Kuldeep Yadav.

India Playing XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill (c), Rishabh Pant (w), Ravindra Jadeja, Dhruv Jurel, Saransh Jain, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna.

Saransh receives his first Test cap after Kuldeep was ruled out with an infection. The change gives India another spin option alongside Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar.

The rest of the side remains unchanged after India's impressive performance in Galle.

Sri Lanka have named an XI featuring Dhananjaya de Silva as captain and Niroshan Dickwella as wicketkeeper.

Sri Lanka Playing XI: Lahiru Udara, Kamil Mishara, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva (c), Sonal Dinusha, Niroshan Dickwella (w), Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando.

The hosts will need a significantly improved performance from their bowling attack after India's batters and spinners dominated large periods of the opening Test.

IND vs SL 2nd Test: India Look To Seal Series

India enter the Colombo Test with a 1-0 lead and will be aiming to complete a series sweep.

Devdutt Padikkal was one of the standout performers in Galle, while Manav Suthar made a major impact with the ball. Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav also played key roles during India's 165-run victory.

With Kuldeep now unavailable, the spotlight will be on debutant Saransh and India's other spinners as the match progresses.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, need a win to draw the series and will be hoping the Colombo surface gives their bowlers greater assistance as the Test moves into its later stages.

With India batting first, the opening sessions could prove crucial in determining how much control Gill's side can establish in the second Test.
